title: Shared work follows the reviewer

slide.title: Caller priority promotes the same shared work
slide.narrative:
- An interactive caller can promote existing shared work without starting another operation. The shared read joins its stored `GitHubWork` before it registers the reader.
- Work scopes keep parent references. This lets pending tasks and requests made after an `await` use a promoted priority.
- The scheduler reads effective priority during `drain`. Promotion alone does not call `drain` or stop active requests. Exclusive ordering and parallel-read conditions still apply.
- In the client, a paced result releases the scheduler slot before a short sleep and another submission. The scheduler controls selection and concurrency; it does not itself enforce rate limits.

fileSummaries.summary: Caller scopes promote shared work, and the scheduler reads effective priority when it selects pending tasks.
One operation serves multiple readers and receives cancellation when its last reader leaves before settlement.
Client work submits requests to the scheduler and waits outside its slot before it submits paced work again.

inlineExplanations.text: `createSharedRead` starts the operation during construction, so `work` exists before a caller reads. Joining changes that existing work; it does not create another operation.
The operation carries this scope across awaits. Nested work keeps a parent reference, so its effective priority can increase when an earlier work scope is promoted.
A user caller can remove the automatic classification even at the same priority. This covers a user joining an automatic foreground refresh without a priority increase.
A supplied scope remains a reference, not a priority snapshot. The client supplies its current scope, so a later promotion can affect pending selection.
Priority does not bypass exclusive ordering. Overlap requires explicit parallel permission and effective interactive priority; an active exclusive task blocks all starts.
Each reader releases its own registration. One reader can cancel without cancelling work that another reader still needs; the last departure signals unfinished work to abort.
The paced attempt has returned before this sleep. The loop later submits the same work scope again, which lets a promotion affect the next attempt without holding a scheduler slot.
